newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS- JUNE 10.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS- JUNE 10.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek general press:

--Laymen and clergy rallied yesterday outside Parliament to protest the chamber's discussion of the Schengen Treaty. A last minute proposal for a roll call vote forced the postponement of a decision, following ugly scenes between police and protestors when they tried to force their way into the building.
--Education ministry employees have placed the hopes of 170,000 university entrance hopefuls on hold with their sudden demands for bonuses, just two weeks before examinations are to get under way.
--President Clinton's new emissary on the Cyprus problem Richard Holbrooke says a "new tragedy" is all too possible for the divided island as both sides "harden their stance".

--The Balkan foreign ministers meeting in Thessaloniki, which began yesterday, has opened the way for a new period of cooperation and security in the sensitive region. "The Balkan peoples can discuss their problems without the interference of foreigners," Foreign Minister Theodoros Pangalos said.

--A new report from the European Parliament has added fat to the Schengen fire, alleging a series of irregularities and violations of privacy in countries where the Schengen treaty is already applied.
--A newspaper investigation reports on who is bidding for a share of the four trillion drachma procurements programme for the Greek military.

--Some 150,000 landlords who do not declare or who under-estimate their income from rentals are the tax department's next target: the landlords have been detected through cross-checks on 1996 tax declaration forms.

--Greece has not yet consolidated the administrative authority to implement Schengen, Spyros Simitis, Frankfurt law professor and head of the research centre for the protection of human rights, says. Simitis is the brother of the Greek prime minister.
--A conference on corruption has revealed that bribery in the public sector is a matter of course: the situation is worsened by an administration which tolerates rather than punishes.

--There's an impressive demand for Greek telecoms organisation OTE's second public offer with initial estimates saying 200,000 investors want OTE shares. --Maria Petrakis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
